key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns hard inverse design into a latent-space search problem by pairing a physics-aware generative decoder with constrained optimization to efficiently find microstructures that match a target response.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical workflow for materials design when direct optimization over microstructure or device geometry is infeasible, expensive, or non-Euclidean.
method: Train a ViT-based encoder and generative decoders to learn a compact latent representation of EBSD microstructures.
Use the decoder as a validity prior and a self-segmenting orientation codec to convert generated images into crystal-plasticity solver inputs.
Optimize the latent variables with MERIDIAN, which combines deep-kernel GP uncertainty, feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On a dataset of about 80,000 EBSD-derived microstructures, the ViT-FMDiT model achieved reconstruction quality reported as FID 27.86 and MS-SSIM 0.178, and with 160 simulations it reduced relative target error by 3%–22% versus seven baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the learned decoder and solver fidelity, so out-of-distribution microstructures or segmentation errors could limit reliability in deployment.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
